title: A localization is a flat algebra
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $T\subseteq R$ a multiplicative subset ($1\in T$, $st\in T$ for $s,t\in T$). Let $\lambda:R\to R'$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings which is a localization of $R$ at $T$: (a) $\lambda(t)$ is a unit for every $t\in T$; (b) every element of $R'$ is $\lambda(r)\lambda(t)^{-1}$ with $r\in R$, $t\in T$; (c) $\lambda(r)=0$ implies $tr=0$ for some $t\in T$ (for instance $R'=T^{-1}R$, the ring of fractions $r/t$, with $\lambda(r)=r/1$). Then $\lambda$ is a flat ring map [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]: $R'$ is a flat $R$-module.
